name: MyPolar 0.4 nozzle
machine_start_gcode:
; Machine coordinates: bed angle C (degrees), radius X, Z. Copied verbatim into the polar G-code.
G90 ; absolute coordinates
M83 ; relative extrusion
M140 S[bed_temperature_initial_layer_single] ; set bed temp
M104 S[nozzle_temperature_initial_layer] ; set extruder temp
G28 ; home all
G1 Z5 F600 ; lift clear of the bed
M190 S[bed_temperature_initial_layer_single] ; wait for bed temp
M109 S[nozzle_temperature_initial_layer] ; wait for extruder temp
G92 E0
machine_end_gcode:
; Machine coordinates, copied verbatim.
G1 E-1.0 F2100 ; retract
G92 E0
M104 S0 ; extruder heater off
M140 S0 ; bed heater off
M107 ; fan off
G91
G1 Z10 F600 ; lift
G90
M84 ; motors off
printer_notes: A polar printer, with a turning bed, a head on one radial line and Z, and a nozzle that does not tilt, printing flat layers. The G-code is in machine coordinates: bed angle C in degrees, radius X from the rotation axis (0 to 100 mm here) and Z, with inverse time feed (G93), for firmware that runs its axes as they are. Set the radius travel, axis letters and bed size to your machine, and calibrate with Calibration > Polar alignment. If your firmware converts Cartesian G-code itself (RepRapFirmware M669 K7, Klipper kinematics: polar), use a Cartesian printer with a round bed centred on the rotation axis instead.
